meta.name: Microsoft Power BI Data Analyst Associate (PL-300)
meta.notes: Initial pack — 12 scenario-style questions across the four PL-300 domains: prepare the data, model the data, visualize and analyze the data, and manage and secure Power BI. keyword-balance pass. v1.1: +10 — append vs merge, bidirectional relationships, CALCULATE, DIVIDE, bookmark toggles, Performance Analyzer, workspace roles, refresh limits, sensitivity labels, Q&A synonyms.

questions.question: An analyst imports a 40-million-row table from a SQL Server database into Power BI. In Power Query they remove several columns and filter the data to the last two years, but refreshes are slow because the full table is pulled before the steps are applied. What should they confirm to ensure these transformations are translated into a single SQL statement executed on the server?
options: That query folding is preserved, so Power Query pushes the column removal and row filter down to the SQL Server source

That incremental refresh is enabled, so only the most recent partition is downloaded on each scheduled refresh — incremental refresh reduces the data volume per run, but it does not push the transformation steps such as the filter down to SQL Server as a single query

That the Remove Columns step is replaced with Choose Columns so the navigator hides the unused fields — swapping these two steps makes no functional difference to Power Query folding behavior; neither step inherently prevents or enables the push-down of the query to the source
That the data source privacy level is set to Public so the mashup engine can freely combine it with other queries
questions.explanation: Query folding is the process by which Power Query translates transformation steps — filters, column selection, grouping, joins — into a native query, a single SQL statement for SQL Server, so the work runs on the source and only the result set is transferred. Keeping the early steps foldable is the key tuning lever in this scenario. Incremental refresh limits which partitions reload but does not by itself fold the in-query steps; Choose Columns versus Remove Columns is cosmetic and both can fold; and privacy levels govern data combination, not this single-source push-down.

questions.question: Before building a model, an analyst wants a quick visual summary in Power Query Editor showing the percentage of valid, error, and empty values in each column, plus the distribution of distinct values. Which feature set should they enable, and what should they know about its default scope?
options: The Query Diagnostics tools on the Tools tab; by default they profile a random five percent sample of the rows — Query Diagnostics trace step execution performance and column distribution of sampled data, not the quality summary of valid, error, and empty values provided by the dedicated Column quality and Column distribution tools
The Column quality, Column distribution, and Column profile tools on the View tab; by default they profile the top 1000 rows, which can be switched to the entire data set
The Merge queries and Append queries commands on the Home tab; by default they profile every related query in the file
The Detect data type and Use first row as headers commands; by default they profile only the columns currently selected
questions.explanation: Power Query Editor's data profiling tools — Column quality, Column distribution, and Column profile — are turned on from the View tab. Column quality shows the percentage of valid, error, and empty values; Column distribution shows distinct and unique counts. By default profiling is based on the top 1000 rows, and the status bar lets you switch to 'Column profiling based on entire data set'. Query Diagnostics traces step performance, Merge and Append combine queries, and Detect data type infers types — none of these produce the quality summary described.

questions.question: A sales fact table holds eight years of history and grows every day. Import refreshes now take hours because every row is reloaded. The analyst wants the dataset to reload only the last 10 days on each scheduled refresh while keeping older data in place. What should they configure?
options: An incremental refresh policy, after creating the RangeStart and RangeEnd date/time parameters and filtering the table by them
A DirectQuery connection to the source so the model never stores any rows and nothing needs to be refreshed
A calculated table that uses DATESINPERIOD to keep only the last 10 days and discards the older history
A scheduled refresh set to run eight times per day so each run processes a smaller slice of the table
questions.explanation: Incremental refresh requires two reserved parameters, RangeStart and RangeEnd, used to filter the table by a date/time column. You then define a policy that stores a chosen amount of history and refreshes only a trailing window — here, 10 days — so Power BI partitions the table and reprocesses just the recent partitions. DirectQuery removes the import but changes query behavior and source load; a calculated table with DATESINPERIOD would drop the history that must be kept; and refreshing more often still reloads the whole table on each run.

questions.question: An analyst inherits a model where a Product dimension is split into separate Product, Subcategory, and Category tables chained one to another, and several measures are slow with ambiguous filter paths. Following Power BI modeling guidance, what is the recommended change?
options: Combine the fact table and every dimension into one flat table so all columns live in a single import table — flattening everything including the category, product, and subcategory columns into the fact table removes the star schema structure and bloats row count with repeated dimensional data

Keep the chained design but set every relationship's cross-filter direction to Both to remove the ambiguity — bidirectional cross-filtering on chained tables does not consolidate the tables; it risks ambiguous filter paths and circular dependencies without reducing the number of tables or improving the schema structure
Collapse the snowflaked Product, Subcategory, and Category tables into one denormalized dimension related directly to the fact table, forming a star schema
Convert each relationship to a many-to-many cardinality so the engine can resolve the longer filter path automatically
questions.explanation: Power BI's recommended pattern is a star schema: a central fact table surrounded by single, denormalized dimension tables joined by one-to-many, single-direction relationships. Collapsing the snowflaked Product, Subcategory, and Category chain into one Product dimension shortens filter paths and improves performance and clarity. Flattening the fact and all dimensions into one table loses the star benefits and bloats the model; setting every relationship to bidirectional invites ambiguity and circular paths; and many-to-many relationships add ambiguity rather than removing it.

questions.question: A model has a dedicated Calendar table related to the Sales table. Time intelligence measures using TOTALYTD and SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR return blank or incorrect values, even though the Calendar table holds a continuous range of dates. What is the most likely fix?
options: Change the Sales table's date column data type to Text so the time intelligence functions can parse it consistently

Add a bidirectional relationship between Sales and Calendar so date filters flow in both directions — bidirectional cross-filtering changes which tables propagate filter context, but it does not supply the continuous date column metadata that DAX time intelligence functions require from a properly marked date table
Create a calculated column in Sales that copies the date, then rebuild the measures against that new column
Use 'Mark as date table' on the Calendar table and select its unique, continuous date column as the date key
questions.explanation: DAX time intelligence functions need a properly marked date table — a table flagged with 'Mark as date table' and a designated unique, continuous date column. Without it, functions such as TOTALYTD and SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR cannot reliably build the date filter context. Changing the column to Text breaks date logic entirely; a bidirectional relationship does not supply the date-table metadata; and copying the date into the fact table does not mark a dimension as the date table.

questions.question: An analyst needs a 'Total Revenue' value that recalculates dynamically as users change slicers and drill through the report, without storing a value on every row of the fact table. Which modeling object should they create?
options: A calculated column, because it is evaluated for each row and stored with the table at refresh time
A measure, because it is evaluated at query time within the current filter context and is not stored row by row
A query parameter, because it captures a single value the user can change before a refresh runs
A calculated table, because it materializes a new table that pre-aggregates the fact rows
questions.explanation: A measure is a DAX calculation evaluated at query time within the prevailing filter context, so it responds to slicers, cross-filtering, and drilldown without being stored row by row — ideal for aggregations such as Total Revenue. A calculated column is computed and stored per row at refresh and does not react to report filters the same way; a query parameter holds a single design-time value; and a calculated table materializes an entire table rather than a context-aware aggregate.

questions.question: An analyst must build a measure that shows each product category's sales as a percentage of the total sales of all categories, and the percentage must stay relative to the full set even when a category slicer is applied. Which approach computes the denominator correctly?
options: Use SUMX over the Sales table alone, because iterating every row already ignores the slicer selection — SUMX still respects the external filter context, so the denominator will shrink to match the selected product or category rather than spanning all categories in the model
Use RELATED to pull a precomputed category total from the dimension table into each fact row
Divide category sales by a denominator built with CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Amount]), ALL(Product[Category])), which removes the category filter
Use the EARLIER function so the measure can reference the category total from an outer row context
questions.explanation: To get a stable grand total, the denominator must ignore the category filter. CALCULATE with ALL(Product[Category]) as a filter argument removes that column's filter context, returning the all-category total regardless of the slicer; dividing category sales by it yields the percentage of total. SUMX still respects the external filter context, RELATED only follows a relationship to fetch a column value, and EARLIER is used for nested row contexts in calculated columns — none of them remove the category filter.

questions.question: Report consumers want to right-click a bar that represents a specific customer and jump to a dedicated page showing that customer's detailed order history, automatically filtered to the customer they selected. Which Power BI feature should the analyst configure?
options: A bookmark that captures the current state of the report and is triggered from a button — a bookmark replays a saved view of the report; it does not pass the customer value selected in a visual as a dynamic filter to a destination page
A report-page tooltip that displays a mini visual when the user hovers over the bar
A slicer synced across pages so a selection made on one page carries over to the detail page
A drillthrough page with the Customer field added to the page's Drillthrough filter well
questions.explanation: A drillthrough page is built by adding a field — here, Customer — to the page's Drillthrough well. Consumers then right-click a data point and choose Drill through to navigate to that page filtered to the selected value. Bookmarks capture and replay report states but do not pass a clicked value as a filter; report-page tooltips appear on hover, not on navigation; and a synced slicer carries an explicit slicer selection, not the right-click context from a visual.

questions.question: An analyst wants a visual that automatically analyzes the data and ranks which categorical factors most increase the likelihood that customer satisfaction is rated 'High'. Which visual is purpose-built for this?
options: The Key influencers visual, which runs built-in analysis to rank the factors that most affect a selected outcome

The Decomposition tree visual, which the user expands manually to explore a measure across chosen dimensions — the decomposition tree lets analysts drill into factors interactively, but it does not run built-in automated analysis to rank which factors most influence a specific outcome
The Q&A visual, which returns a visual in response to a typed natural-language question
A clustered column chart with conditional formatting applied to the satisfaction column
questions.explanation: The Key influencers visual runs automated analysis to identify and rank the factors that most influence a chosen metric or outcome value — for example, what drives a 'High' satisfaction rating. The Decomposition tree is an interactive drill visual that the user expands manually and does not rank influencers automatically; Q&A answers typed natural-language questions; and a clustered column chart with conditional formatting shows values but performs no influence analysis.

questions.question: Each regional sales manager must open the same published report but see only the rows for their own region. The analyst wants to enforce this in the dataset rather than building separate reports per region. What should they implement?
options: Separate workspaces per region, granting each manager Viewer access only to their own region's workspace
Row-level security: define roles with a DAX filter on the region table, then assign each manager to their role in the Power BI service
Sensitivity labels from Microsoft Purview applied to the report so each region's content is classified differently
Object-level security that hides the Region column from the report so managers cannot see other regions
questions.explanation: Row-level security (RLS) restricts data at the row level. The analyst defines roles in Power BI Desktop with a DAX filter expression — often using USERPRINCIPALNAME() or a mapping table — and then assigns users or groups to those roles in the Power BI service. Per-region workspaces would mean maintaining many copies of the report; sensitivity labels govern classification and protection, not row filtering; and object-level security hides whole tables or columns from a role, not specific rows per user.

questions.question: A report is published to the Power BI service and connects to a SQL Server database running in the company's on-premises datacenter. Scheduled refresh fails with a message that the data source cannot be reached. What is required to enable scheduled refresh against this source?
options: Re-publish the report with the storage mode changed to DirectQuery, which removes any need to reach the source during refresh
Move the workspace into a Premium capacity, because scheduled refresh of on-premises sources is a Premium-only feature
Install and configure an on-premises data gateway in standard mode, then bind the dataset's data source to that gateway in the service
Save the source credentials inside the PBIX file before publishing so the service can authenticate directly to the server
questions.explanation: The Power BI service runs in the cloud and cannot reach an on-premises database directly. An on-premises data gateway in standard (enterprise) mode, installed on a machine inside the corporate network, bridges the connection; you then map the dataset's data source to that gateway in the service to enable scheduled refresh. DirectQuery to an on-premises source still requires a gateway; scheduled refresh of on-premises data is not Premium-only; and credentials are configured against the data source in the service, not embedded in the PBIX file.

questions.question: An analyst has finished a workspace containing several related reports and dashboards and must distribute them to about 200 business users who should consume the content read-only through a single, easy-to-navigate experience. What is the recommended distribution method?
options: Add all 200 users as Members of the workspace so they can open every item directly
Share each report individually with the 200 users and resend the links whenever a report changes
Export each report to PDF and email the files to the 200 users on a recurring schedule
Publish a Power BI app from the workspace and grant the audience access to it
questions.explanation: A Power BI app is the recommended way to distribute curated content to a broad audience. You publish the app from the workspace, choose which items to include, and grant audiences access; consumers get a single, packaged, read-only experience with built-in navigation. Adding 200 users as workspace Members gives them edit permissions and exposes work in progress; sharing reports one by one is unmanageable at scale; and exporting to PDF loses interactivity and data freshness.

questions.question: An analyst has January, February and March sales extracts with identical columns and wants one combined table. Separately, the Sales table needs Product-category columns added by matching on ProductID. Which Power Query operations satisfy these two needs respectively?
options: Merge queries for the monthly extracts, then append queries to bring in the category columns afterwards
Append queries for the monthly extracts; merge queries for the ProductID lookup
Group By for the monthly extracts; transpose the Product table to attach its columns
Union in DAX for the monthly extracts; RELATED in Power Query for the category columns
questions.explanation: Append stacks tables with the same schema vertically (more rows) — the monthly extracts case. Merge joins two tables on a key to bring in columns horizontally (more columns) — the ProductID lookup. Group By aggregates rather than combines; transpose flips rows/columns; UNION and RELATED are DAX functions, not Power Query operations, and RELATED doesn't exist in the query editor.

questions.question: In a star schema, an analyst changes the Date-to-Sales relationship's cross-filter direction from Single to Both to make one visual work. What is the main risk of this change?
options: Ambiguous filter paths and degraded performance as filters propagate in both directions across the model
The relationship is automatically deleted the next time the dataset is refreshed in the service
Row-level security definitions stop being evaluated for any table on the Many side
All measures referencing the Date table return blank until each one is rewritten with CALCULATE
questions.explanation: Bidirectional cross-filtering lets filters flow from the fact table back into dimensions, which can create ambiguous paths in models with multiple relationships and adds filter-propagation work that hurts performance — which is why Single direction is the star-schema default. Refresh doesn't delete relationships, RLS still evaluates (bidirectional relationships actually need extra care with RLS, not abandonment), and measures don't blank out.

questions.question: A measure must show total sales for the selected period but ONLY for orders shipped to the 'West' region, regardless of any Region slicer selection. Which DAX pattern does this?
options: Total West Sales = SUMX(Sales, Sales[Amount] * (Sales[Region] = "West"))
Total West Sales = FILTER(SUM(Sales[Amount]), Sales[Region] = "West")
Total West Sales = CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Amount]), Sales[Region] = "West")
Total West Sales = SUM(Sales[Amount]) WHERE Sales[Region] = "West"
questions.explanation: CALCULATE evaluates an expression in a modified filter context; the boolean filter argument replaces any existing filter on Sales[Region], so 'West' wins over slicer selections. FILTER takes a table, not a scalar, as its first argument, so option B is invalid syntax; the SUMX trick multiplies by TRUE/FALSE but does not override an external Region filter; DAX has no WHERE clause.

questions.question: A 'Sales per Unit' measure throws division-by-zero errors for products with no units sold. Which is the recommended fix?
options: Sales per Unit = IFERROR([Total Sales] / [Total Units], "N/A")
Sales per Unit = [Total Sales] / ([Total Units] + 0.0001)
Wrap the visual in a tooltip so the error is hidden from report consumers at display time
Sales per Unit = DIVIDE([Total Sales], [Total Units])
questions.explanation: DIVIDE is the purpose-built safe-division function: it returns BLANK (or an optional alternate result) when the denominator is zero, and it is optimized by the engine. IFERROR catches the error but is slower and returning the text "N/A" breaks the measure's numeric type; padding the denominator distorts every result slightly; hiding errors in the UI leaves the model broken.

questions.question: A report page must let users switch between a chart view and a table view of the same data using two buttons. Which Power BI features implement this pattern?
options: Bookmarks that capture visual visibility states from the Selection pane, assigned to the buttons' actions
Two separate report pages connected by drillthrough filters configured on the table visual
A what-if parameter whose values toggle each visual's transparency between 0 and 100 percent
Small multiples on the chart, configured so one of the multiples renders as a table
questions.explanation: The toggle pattern is built from the Selection pane (hide one visual, show the other), bookmarks capturing each visibility state, and buttons whose action is each bookmark. Drillthrough navigates to a filtered detail page rather than swapping visuals in place; what-if parameters drive measure values, not visibility; small multiples split one visual by a category and cannot render a table.

questions.question: A published report has become slow and the analyst must find out which visual or DAX query is responsible. Which Power BI Desktop tool provides per-visual durations for DAX query, visual display and other operations?
options: The Sync Slicers pane
Performance Analyzer
Query Diagnostics in Power Query
The Enhanced Metadata format setting
questions.explanation: Performance Analyzer records each visual's DAX query time, rendering time and 'other' overhead per interaction, and lets you copy the slow query for deeper analysis in DAX Studio. Query Diagnostics profiles Power Query refresh steps, not report interactions; Sync Slicers coordinates slicers across pages; the enhanced metadata format is a file-format setting unrelated to profiling.

questions.question: A colleague must be able to edit and publish reports in a workspace but must NOT be able to add or remove other users. Which workspace role fits?
options: Viewer
Admin
Member
Contributor
questions.explanation: Contributors can create, edit, publish and delete content in the workspace but cannot manage access. Members can additionally add users (with lower permissions) and publish/update apps; Admins control everything including deleting the workspace; Viewers have read-only interaction. Role-permission mapping is a recurring 'manage and secure' exam item.

questions.question: A dataset in a workspace on shared (Pro) capacity must be refreshed as often as possible from an on-premises source. What is the maximum number of scheduled refreshes per day?
questions.explanation: Shared capacity allows up to 8 scheduled refreshes per day per dataset; Premium/Fabric capacities raise this to 48. One per day is the default single slot people often start with, and 24/48 are the Premium-tier figures candidates confuse with Pro. (Refreshes via the REST API or change to DirectQuery are the routes around the limit.)

questions.question: Compliance requires that when users export report data to Excel, the file remains encrypted and usable only by authorized employees. Which Power BI capability provides this?
options: Row-level security roles defined in the dataset and assigned in the service
Workspace Viewer role assignments combined with disabling the print option
Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels with protection applied to the report
A private endpoint connecting the Power BI service to the corporate network
questions.explanation: Sensitivity labels follow the data: when a labeled report is exported to Excel or PDF, the label's encryption and access restrictions travel with the file, so only authorized users can open it. RLS limits which rows a user sees inside Power BI but exported data loses that protection context; viewer roles and private endpoints control access to the service, not to files after export.

questions.question: Business users want to type questions like 'total sales by region last quarter' directly on a report page and get a visual answer. The data team also wants 'revenue' to be understood as the Sales Amount field. What should the analyst configure?
options: A Q&A visual on the page, plus a 'revenue' synonym on the Sales Amount field in Q&A setup
A decomposition tree with Sales Amount as the target and region as an explain-by field
A smart narrative visual configured with custom values referencing the Sales Amount measure
A key influencers visual analyzing what drives Sales Amount across regional segments
questions.explanation: The Q&A visual answers natural-language questions, and Q&A setup lets modelers teach it vocabulary — adding 'revenue' as a synonym for Sales Amount so business terms resolve to model fields. Decomposition trees, smart narratives and key influencers are AI visuals too, but none of them accepts free-text questions from the user.
